In last month's Democratic primary, Frisch defeated Sol Sandoval, who'd been considered the frontrunner to take on Boebert, with 42.4 percent of the vote to her 41.9 percent — a narrow margin, but just outside the point that would have triggered a recount. Both Sandoval and Alex Walker, who earned 15.7 percent of the vote (after launching his campaign with an ad showing a Boebert lookalike spraying faux sewage from a hose), have pledged to stump on his behalf.

When telling his origin story, Frisch focuses on elements that contradict the image of a rich, entitled Aspenite that Boebert and her minions are likely to push. "I spent my first five years on an Indian reservation in northeast Montana," he notes. His father worked in the public health service, went on to become a career OB/GYN and "spent the last four or five years before he retired working for Planned Parenthood, to make sure the next generation of health-care providers had the proper training." And after the family moved to Minneapolis, he says, "my mom helped with the public-schools system" on issues such as diversifying the student mix at various institutions.

During his youth, Frisch got into ski racing, which inspired him to enroll at the University of Colorado Boulder in 1986. His ski-racing career was short-circuited by injury, "but I decided to stay, because it's obviously a great institution," he says. He subsequently headed to New York City, where "I fell into working in one of the first socially responsible investment funds. It wasn't so much green technology, because there wasn't as much of it then, but helping people avoid certain industries when they were putting their money to work," he notes. From there, "I got involved with global interest rates and the financial markets — spent eight years traveling the world and went to forty or fifty different countries."

After 911, Frisch decided to move back to Colorado and "ended up meeting a gal on the Western Slope and convinced her that if we wanted to build a family, we should possibly look at Aspen for a place to go, because of the business opportunities," he recalls. He and wife Katy settled in Aspen in 2003, and in addition to building that family — their two children are Quintessa, fifteen, and Felix, sixteen — they became embedded in the community. Katy "runs a family manufacturing business" and is currently president of the local school board, and Frisch spent eight years, from 2011 to 2019, as a member of the Aspen City Council, where "90 percent of my focus was about affordable housing, which is a really important aspect here in Aspen," he says. He also did some substitute teaching during COVID because of his belief that students learn better in a classroom.

Frisch's latest chapter began unfolding this past November. "After Boebert said something disparaging, mean, petty, obnoxious, bigoted, I pulled out the 2020 election results for six or seven people in the House — people like Marjorie Taylor Greene and Matt Gaetz. I saw that most of them had 65-to-75 percent win ratios in 2020, but Boebert had only won 51 percent of CD3 — it was 51 to 46 percent" over challenger Diane Mitsch Bush," he notes. "I thought, if 5 percent of the people had switched their vote, Boebert would have lost."

In the two years that followed, the math became a little more difficult, with the 3rd Congressional District's percentage of Republican voters rising substantially after new lines were drawn. But Frisch says he was prepared for that: "I assumed redistricting was coming, so I thought we needed 10 percent to switch. But I still see her as electorally weak, and I thought that if a moderate Democrat could get past the primary, he could build a coalition with Democrats, independents and the rational Republican crowd. So 10 percent of those prior voters is the holy grail of how someone can win."

At that time, Frisch was registered as unaffiliated, but he switched to the Democratic Party in December. "I had some core Democratic values," he stresses. "The driving force is who sits on the U.S. Supreme Court. Taxes and regulations come and go, but it's obviously relevant how important the Supreme Court is. I know I'm not applying for a job that has a direct influence on who's on the court, but I'd rather have Democrats than Republicans making those decisions."

Nonetheless, he admits that "if there had been a normal Republican running, like Don Coram, I wouldn't have gotten into this race, because I don't think a Democrat can defeat what I would call a mainline Republican in this district." Indeed, he adds, "The only reason I got into this conversation was because of Boebert, who's extremist in a couple of ways. She's voted against the financial interests of our district and she has an extremist view of a number of things, including being really pro-Putin. And I don't need 50 percent of Republicans to vote for me. I only need 10 percent."

Frisch announced his candidacy in February, and while he had the benefit of his personal financial resources, "We worked really hard," he recalls. "My wife and I had a nineteen-foot camper trailer, and we turned it into a mobile billboard — the 'Beat Boebert Buggy.' We drove to dozens of communities, including a lot of places that hadn't had a candidate come through when they could remember; we'd stop in front of schools to let people know how focused I was on education and just talk to them. And we won despite having a demographic that wasn't right up the alley of the traditional Democratic base because I was able to get in front of people and let them know I'm a kind, caring person who's a good listener, and my background doesn't conform to the stereotypes that people were concerned about."

The top issues for Frisch are "the economy and inflation. Everything costs too damn much, whether it's rent, a pound of beef or, obviously, a gallon of gas. We'll be going on some kind of economic-recovery tour and help people to understand that I've had a lot of success in business, and that type of success will be needed to focus on the economy." He's also concerned about making sure health care and educational opportunities are available in rural communities as well as larger metropolitan areas, plus issues related to water rights and energy. As he sees it, "we need to have a true transition from legacy production to future production, but we also need to respect people from those legacy industries. A great example of this transition is a 150-year-old steel mill in Pueblo that's 90 percent solar-powered. So Colorado has a lot of examples of how to do this transition properly. But it's important to realize that when these jobs change, people need to be moving to jobs that pay well."

"I think a lot of people know that her sweet spot is her Twitter account and being on cable news, where I think Fox News is the most liberal venue where she speaks," he says. Republican U.S. Rep. Lauren Boebert and her Democratic challenger, Adam Frisch, are scheduled to face off in early September at a debate in Grand Junction, their campaigns confirmed, but Frisch, a former Aspen city council member, said he hopes the Republican incumbent agrees to additional meetings in the run-up to the November election.

On Monday, Frisch challenged Boebert to debate five times — in Grand Junction at Western Slope advocacy group Club 20's fall meeting, and in other cities throughout the sprawling 3rd Congressional District, including Pueblo, Alamosa, Durango and Rifle, where Boebert operated Shooters Grill until earlier this month when the gun-themed restaurant closed after losing its lease.

“I will debate Lauren Boebert anytime, anywhere, on any issue," Frisch said in a release.

Boebert's campaign told Colorado Politics in an email that the congresswoman has accepted and looks forward to attending the match-up at Club 20's meeting but didn't respond to an inquiry about scheduling additional debates.

"She also looks forward to winning this election in the fall so she can help fire Nancy Pelosi," the campaign said in the email.

Frisch told Colorado Politics he's happy to talk about any issue Boebert wants to discuss, including the Second Amendment and energy independence.

"I’m not surprised that she’s scared to debate me, to get in front of her voters," he said. "I think one of the core duties of a public elected official is to go talk to everybody, not just show up in the most friendly of places."

Club 20's 3rd CD debate takes place in the middle of a day of debates featuring legislative, statewide and congressional candidates running to represent parts of the Western Slope.

Traditionally, the meeting's debates have served as the unofficial kick-off to Colorado's fall campaign season, though in the past two election cycles several Democrats running in top-ticket races — including Jared Polis, making his successful run for governor in 2018, and John Hickenlooper, on the way to winning a U.S. Senate seat in 2020 — have skipped the debates.

Also in 2020, neither Boebert, who was seeking her first term, nor her Democratic opponent, former state Rep. Diane Mitsch Bush, showed up for the confab, with Mitsch Bush citing COVID safety concerns and Boebert declining to participate if she couldn't submit a prerecorded video answering questions provided in advance. The two didn't manage to schedule any other debates, and Boebert went on to win the Republican-leaning seat by about 6 percentage points.

| [ ](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/20348?t=6&akid=3938%2E878179%2Eo_9JQu) Dear friends,

I got a favor to ask you. Not for me. For the country. [**I want you to donate to a campaign. Not mine. Josh Riley’s. And to Voter Protection Project, too.**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/20348?t=7&akid=3938%2E878179%2Eo_9JQu) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Josh Riley and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $5 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/20349?t=8&akid=3938%2E878179%2Eo_9JQu)
---
[CONTRIBUTE $25 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/20350?t=9&akid=3938%2E878179%2Eo_9JQu)
[CONTRIBUTE $50 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/20351?t=10&akid=3938%2E878179%2Eo_9JQu)
[CONTRIBUTE $100 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/20352?t=11&akid=3938%2E878179%2Eo_9JQu)
[Or a custom donation »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/20348?t=12&akid=3938%2E878179%2Eo_9JQu)
Who? Glad you asked. Josh was my General Counsel on the Senate Judiciary Committee from 2011 – 2014, and is now running for an open House seat in upstate New York. Even during a period of partisan gridlock, Josh and I successfully got two bills through Congress and signed by the President. One created new rights for survivors of domestic violence. The other provided new funding for addiction treatment and mental health programs.

Josh grew up in Upstate New York in a working-class family. His entire career has been dedicated to making life better for people who don’t have people fighting for them. Get to know Josh and what he stands for [**HERE**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/19824?t=13&akid=3938%2E878179%2Eo_9JQu). I was fortunate to have had many, many brilliant, dedicated staffers during my years in the Senate. None was better than Josh. And I can’t think of one who would make a more effective member of Congress.

More often than not, I was the best prepared member of the Judiciary Committee. That’s because I took my work very seriously and so did Josh. That said, we had fun. Please go to his [**website**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/19824?t=14&akid=3938%2E878179%2Eo_9JQu) to get to know Josh and what he believes and will be fighting for.

Josh’s seat is a new one, created during redistricting. In a year where every seat will count, this is a tossup district that is a MUST-win for Democrats.

Thanks for your attention.

Al

**P.S.** No other former staff member of mine is running for Congress. So, this is the last one of these!

# FBI manhunt for Gaetz supporter who left terrifying voicemail threatening to kill his opponent
Rebekah Jones
---
| A Matt Gaetz supporter from Shalimar, Florida is currently wanted by the FBI for threatening to kill Gaetz’ opponent, Rebekah Jones, and her family [in a chilling voicemail](https://thepoliticalmatrix.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c3bea68b6a04118d41358241a&id=e2a3743a24&e=10b14e738f) left on her cell phone last week.

“I’m going to kill you. I’m going to kill your whole family. You’re going to die motherfucker,” the caller said.
The man harassed the personal cell phone of Jones and her husband over a period of three days last week. He did not block or hide is number.

The threats came about the same time that Matt Gaetz became embroiled in yet another controversy concerning sexually inappropriate behavior, this time with comments he made at a conservative convention about women and reproductive freedom – themes evident in the wanted-man’s texts to Jones.
“Plus women don’t belong as Governors or anyone like that bc y’all have too many personalities and too emotional to handle big decisions in life!” one of the messages read.

The FBI began searching for the man in cooperation with the Okaloosa County Sheriff’s Department Thursday, July 21, 2022. As of July 30, he is still at-large.

Jones announced the FBI search at a women’s rights rally in Tampa Saturday, where she was joined by Hillsborough County Commissioners Pat Kemp and Kimberly Overman, St. Petersburg City Council Chair Gina Driscoll, President of the Democratic Progressive Caucus of Tampa Bay Alex Khalel and Soil and Water Conservation Board member Dr. Sonja Brookins.

“I’ve gotten a lot of threats,” Jones said at the rally. “That’s what happens when you take on a corrupt governor and then a corrupt congressman. But this one was serious. This one scared me.”

Jones has been the subject of a targeted harassment campaign online since May 2020, led principally by Christina Pushaw, Ron DeSantis’ Nazi-connected press secretary, who notably was hired after a court in Maryland issued a restraining on Jones’ behalf and Pushaw was later criminally charged with violating it.

More recently, Pushaw and a Democratic spoiler candidate from another part of the state have been cooperating online in a smear campaign targeting Jones, rape-shaming, slut-shaming and making sexually-charged comments about Jones online.

The extent of their cooperation was revealed by a former data architect and cyber security specialist from Google, the details of which were just recently leaked online and can be [viewed in this 176-page ethics complaint filed against her](https://thepoliticalmatrix.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c3bea68b6a04118d41358241a&id=27765631ad&e=10b14e738f).

The failing campaign of New York City cooperate attorney Margaret “Peggy” Schiller has been exposed as a sham campaign working on behalf of Ron DeSantis, who has been obsessed with Rebekah Jones for more than two years, and Matt Gaetz.

Jones, who is heavily favored to win both her primary election in August and the general election against Matt Gaetz in November, maintains her status as a legally protected whistleblower after exposing COVID_19 data manipulation by Ron DeSantis’ administration in 2020. Jones gained international notoriety, won national awards, and became known as Florida’s resident COVID-19 expert and one of [the most trusted sources](https://thepoliticalmatrix.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c3bea68b6a04118d41358241a&id=3721efa481&e=10b14e738f) for science information in the country.

July 30 also marked [National Whistleblower Day](https://thepoliticalmatrix.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c3bea68b6a04118d41358241a&id=47bbc64c7e&e=10b14e738f), an event Jones was honored at in both 2021 and 2022. Jones also won “Whistleblower of the Year” for [2020](https://thepoliticalmatrix.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c3bea68b6a04118d41358241a&id=ad75588123&e=10b14e738f), a title given this year to [whistleblower Reality Winner](https://thepoliticalmatrix.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c3bea68b6a04118d41358241a&id=d26fe813c0&e=10b14e738f).

Jones decided to run against Matt Gaetz in Florida’s 1st Congressional District, in the area she grew up, after learning about the FBI sex trafficking investigating Matt Gaetz is currently the target of. Jones turned her own grandfather into the FBI in 2019 for sex trafficking in the Philippines. He was later arrested and imprisoned, where he died earlier this year.

A call for Gaetz to make a public statement condemning the threats has gone unanswered, even though Jones issued such a statement in 2021 when Matt Gaetz was receiving threats:

name: Governor Ron DeSantis
subject: I'm here to lead
body:
I’m truly grateful for staunch allies like you. [](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/BC.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c210334%7c0554%7c8%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz%7c805&wdmdk=%2bLpDm9H1RVQvjq2jstR0Bw&sysid=1)
**[](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c39132%7c210334%7c805%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=CW%2fjvJVxpu%2firYo6Wt%2fkWw&sysid=1)**

Friend,
I’m truly grateful for staunch allies like you.
_**It wouldn’t be right to go another day without expressing my gratitude for your unwavering support of my re-election campaign.**_
As Election Day nears, I’m taking some time to think back over the events that unfolded during my first term as Governor.
Do you remember Biden’s Democrat allies in the legacy media running to cover for Dr. Fauci by supporting unscientific lockdowns and the harmful masking of our children?
Or the Biden administration blatantly and disgracefully colluding with Big Tech to silence free speech and cancel all dissent during the pandemic?
_Fortunately, they were not the only ones with access to COVID data ..._
As Governor of Florida, I reached out to and spoke with some of the best scientists and doctors in the world at Harvard, Stanford, and Oxford to assess the necessity of the Left’s destructive lockdown policies.
**The data showed the Left’s draconian policies were failures, and I kept Florida open. And I’m glad I did.**
**Every American has a right to work.**
**Every business has a right to operate.**
That’s why I stepped in and stopped local governments from restricting people from working or operating a business. [_**Do you support my decision to keep Florida open? Stand with me now. >>>**_](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c39133%7c210334%7c805%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=MVQ8Ehgec3vBLiB6z8zajA&sysid=1)
I even issued pardons for those who were threatened by local governments with jail and ridiculous fines for operating during the pandemic.
I put my entire political career on the line to Keep Florida Free. _**I fought back.**_
It showed you exactly the kind of leader I am. I don’t cower with fear about what the media may say -- _I just lead_.
In 2019, when I was inaugurated as Florida’s 46th Governor, I didn’t let the grass grow under my feet before turning the Tallahassee establishment upside down.
I immediately fulfilled several of my key campaign promises to Floridians, including:
✅ Changing the Florida Supreme Court for a generation by appointing three rock-solid conservative justices.
✅ Signing the largest expansion of school choice in the nation, giving parents greater freedom to choose the education that best meets their child’s needs.
✅ Restoring election integrity by holding election officials accountable by accepting the resignation of Broward County Supervisor of Elections Brenda Snipes from public office, as well as suspending Palm Beach County Election Supervisor Susan Bucher.
✅ Suspending Broward County Sheriff Scott Israel for his failure to protect the students at Marjorie Stoneman Douglas High School during the massacre at Parkland in 2018.
Of course, making these moves during my first few days in office was just a preview of what I set out to accomplish.
**Over my first three years, I’ve continued to steer Florida to a strong, safe, prosperous future with liberty as my guide and the Constitutions as my north star.**
[_**Do you think Florida is headed in the right direction? Rush in any amount now to keep our accomplishments going for another four years!**_](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c39134%7c210334%7c805%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=I06M1opEiSnTpF%2fDbyAOJw&sysid=1)
I refuse to simply kick the can down the road or seek out the path of least resistance when it comes to doing the right thing.
I certainly don’t set my priorities according to what is preferred by Silicon Valley’s CEOs, Big Tech’s shady algorithms, or the corrupt media’s agenda!
I refuse to bow to pressure from the Biden administration, kiss the ring of power-hungry government bureaucrats like Fauci, or follow orders from woke corporations who want to dictate to us how to live and what to think.
**I was elected to lead, not to follow.**
As was the case when I was in the U.S. Navy, my mission has always been to advocate for the people I serve.
I’m proud that because of my work these last few years, Florida is known as _the freest state in the country._
Yet rather than celebrate our economy, our school children being freed of compulsory masking, and the influx of overtaxed Americans who are voting with their feet to move to Florida, I am being attacked by my Democrat opponents.
I know you understand that coordinated attacks and vitriol against a successful conservative Republican like me is business as usual from the lockdown Democrats. It’s pathetic to see my political opponents and detractors whine about my record of accomplishments.
**As Governor of Florida, I’ll never stop defending the pro-liberty, pro-free market policies that make Florida the beachhead of freedom for the nation.**
My re-election campaign sent SHOCK WAVES through the Democrat media complex when we announced a $5 MILLION ad reservation targeting Hispanic voters.
With the Biden regime publicly cozying up to communist dictators in Cuba and Venezuela, you can be sure every victim of communism across the state is more willing than ever to reject the Democrat Party's choice for Governor this November.
**I’m going to battle for every vote.**
As you may remember, I narrowly won by a margin of just 0.4% four years ago during my first race for Governor!
We truly must be prepared for another knock-down, drag-out fight.
Now, with just months to go until Election Day, I’m asking you to stand with me again by making another generous contribution to my campaign today.
With November fast approaching, I’m hoping you can double your most generous gift.
[**[PLEDGE YOUR GIFT NOW]**](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c39145%7c210334%7c805%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=HL3W6KDbieKltsy1WLSvFw&sysid=1)
Regardless of the amount, I simply must have your continued support to be ready to respond to the next round of distortions and lies my Biden-loving opponents hurl at me.
_Friend, I’m incredibly grateful to you for your continued support._
No matter the amount, I thank you in advance for continuing to stand with me as I lead by example and fight back against the heavy hand of Biden’s big government.
For Florida,
Ron DeSantis
[](https://click.americanupdate.com/Pages/Click.aspx?ghff34ghj=01%7c39132%7c210334%7c805%7cqcjvyyvf12%40tznvy.pbz&wdmdk=CW%2fjvJVxpu%2firYo6Wt%2fkWw&sysid=1 "DONATE

name: Ron DeSantis
subject: Have you been to CA lately?
body:
| | | [](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60915253:6q3eNkVNi:m:1:3253819041:65A4BFD5CF112FD935FDDF5792A5AA69:r)

Peter, Over the past three years, **we have been called to make choices and answer questions we did not expect.**

Questions about how, in a world that seemed frightening and different, we were going to raise our kids, continue to put food on the table, and care for our communities?

And questions that feel further out now like, how does our government interact with its citizenry in a time of crisis?

How is our government -- one of the people, by the people, for the people -- meant to protect life, but not stifle liberty?

_In crisis, do we foster freedom? Or do we force our citizens down?_

Well, over the past three years I believe we have had the truth revealed about those two vastly different approaches. Not in an academic textbook or in a theoretical debate, but in the harsh reality of governing during COVID. You could not find two more starkly different examples than the free state of Florida and the woke tyranny of Gavin Newsom's California.

It isn't hard to understand why the Governor of California wants to talk about Florida. It's part of the one topic he tries to focus on: _**Anything but California.**_

Let's take a look at the record of the "liberal elite" in California:
1. They locked their kids out of public schools at the behest of the teachers' unions.
2. They forced small businesses to close with many never to re-open again.
3. They hobbled law enforcement and allowed drugs and crime to destroy their cities.

Everything on that list is a tragedy, and it's only made worse by the disregard and disrespect shown by leaders like Gavin Newsom. The idea of locking down your citizens and then darting off to the fanciest restaurant in the state to rub their noses in it.

It's wrong, it's disgusting, and it's no surprise that every day driving around Florida I see more and more California license plates as a result.

**In Florida, we didn't bludgeon our people with government mandates; we lifted people up -- protecting their jobs, their businesses, and their kids' education.**
**[Help us keep Florida free in November>>>](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60915253:6q3eNkVNi:m:1:3253819041:65A4BFD5CF112FD935FDDF5792A5AA69:r "Help us keep Florida free
in November >>>")**
We didn't lock business owners out of their livelihoods and we didn't lock people out of their jobs.

**In Florida we didn't turn a blind eye to crime and drugs, we put criminals behind bars, and we kept our streets safe.**

Gavin Newsom doesn't want to talk about California, and I don't blame him. But the reality is, there are plenty of woke liberal billionaires on Gavin Newsom's speed dial who do not want to see individual freedom succeed. **_They don't want to see it succeed in Florida or anywhere else._**

Because if it succeeds, it shows everyone that the top down nanny-state tyranny of California is avoidable -- Free people making their own decisions are better off than a locked down citizenry dictated to by elitists.

That's why I need your help. Gavin Newsom, funded by Hollywood liberals, Big Tech billionaires, and who knows who else is running ads in Florida. _**I need your help to fight back.**_ **On our side are free people who care to stay that way. On their side is everyone who thinks they know better.**

**Show them that we intend to stay free: [Make a donation right now](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60915253:6q3eNkVNi:m:1:3253819041:65A4BFD5CF112FD935FDDF5792A5AA69:r "Make a donation right now") to help us fight back. You can use this** **[secure link](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60915253:6q3eNkVNi:m:1:3253819041:65A4BFD5CF112FD935FDDF5792A5AA69:r "secure link")**.

Sincerely,__

Hello,
It was Ben Franklin who, when asked what form of government the constitutional convention had produced, said: “A republic, if you can keep it.”
Donald Trump’s election sealed the deal for me to retire after nearly 4 decades in the U.S. Navy. Having been in uniform for every President since Jimmy Carter, I showed my respect for Mr. Trump with my feet. I was done. It was apparent that the next four years would not go well.
Unfortunately, putting himself before his country culminated when Trump and his fellow Republicans planned, cajoled accomplices, then launched a domestic insurrection on the U.S. Capitol. Five lives were lost, and the nation’s innocence, as well. And it ain’t over.
January 6th set a precedent that leadership in a political party will condone political violence. **To this day, GOP members who continue to perpetuate the Big Lie are a direct threat to our democracy.** An opportunity to come clean for my opponent, Senator Chuck Grassley, who voted against Trump’s impeachment and tried to block a bipartisan commission from investigating the attack, still has yet to occur.
The Republican party needs to cull its ranks of the active insurrectionists. Every single person involved in the January 6 attack needs to be held accountable for their actions, including sitting members of Congress who participated in the planning and execution of the insurrection.
**I’m running for the U.S. Senate against Senator Chuck Grassley because I place nation over baseless insurrection. It is a decision not entirely unlike the time of Lincoln. One does not serve the nation in military service to watch idly while it is dismembered by the likes of Donald Trump and his accomplices, to include Chuck Grassley.**
Mitch McConnell and his Super PACs are raising boatloads to spend against me. I am the ultimate “hard target” for the Republicans, but to get elected, **I need your help. I’m not taking money from corporate PACs – instead, I’m relying entirely on grassroots donors _like you_.**

The Democrats are spending MILLIONS

Peter,

Did you catch my interview on Fox News?

It was great to share my story and talk about the incredible momentum behind my campaign for U.S. Senate.

I'm taking on a 30 year incumbent because I believe Washingtonians deserve someone in the Senate who will fight for the issues they care about in their daily lives.

_**Recent polls show me surging ahead, and the Democrats are so scared I 'll flip Washington red that they're spending MILLIONS to try to stop my momentum.**_

I'm doing everything I can to stand up against the career politicians, but I can't win this fight alone. While the Democrats have mega-donors and dark money funding my opponent, I rely on my grassroots supporters like YOU, Peter. [](https://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916805:6w69TkVaN:m:1:3317145305:82495756DA48CFA4FCDBD56CF9D04972:r)
[**
Please, can you help my campaign by chipping in any amount?**](https://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916805:6w69TkVaN:m:1:3317145305:82495756DA48CFA4FCDBD56CF9D04972:r)

As a veterans advocate and triage nurse, I have spent my whole life serving my community. Now, I'm ready to continue that service from the U.S. Senate.

Are you with me?
**[**SUPPORT MY CAMPAIGN**](https://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916805:6w69TkVaN:m:1:3317145305:82495756DA48CFA4FCDBD56CF9D04972:r)**

---

Thank you,

Tiffany Smiley

* * *
**Our country needs leadership, Friend.**
We need someone who will stand up and work to solve our nation's problems. I'm a proven leader, I've stood up to the DC bureaucrats at the VA to pave the way for ALL veterans to receive the care and treatment they deserve when they return home. Our veterans are willing to pay the ultimate price for our everyday freedoms. But when they come back home, their service is often overlooked by our very own government.
After serving our nation and laying their lives on the line overseas, our veterans should **NOT** have to beg to get the care they deserve here at home. We need to do better for those who defend our nation, Friend.
**That's why I'm running for Senate**
[**If you agree we need to stand up for our nation 's heroes, will you chip in to help me reach my major upcoming goal? I need your support, Friend!**](https://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916806:6w69TkVaN:m:1:3317145305:82495756DA48CFA4FCDBD56CF9D04972:r)

subject: Now they’re after our Doctors
body:
[](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916970:6F0Q8kVNs:m:1:3253819041:8FDAE57390781D67EB95D6DD13747EA2:r "REVOKED") Peter: First, they firebombed our medical offices. Then they tried to ban us on Google. Now, they're coming after our doctor's licenses. Just because we encourage life over abortion. The Left knows no bounds in stopping our efforts to operate our ministry to save the lives of preborn boys and girls. And if we are unable to fight back, **this WILL SHUT US DOWN FOR GOOD.** **[If we are going to continue providing a safe place for women in crisis to receive life-saving medical care, then we need you to chip in $25, $50, or $100 today to help us fight back.](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916970:6F0Q8kVNs:m:1:3253819041:8FDAE57390781D67EB95D6DD13747EA2:r "If
we are going to continue providing a safe place for women in crisis to receive life-saving medical care, then we need you to chip in $25, $50, or $100
today to help us fight back.")** During CompassCare's 42 years of offering compassionate care to women facing an unplanned pregnancy, we've faced a lot of attempts to shut us down. But this latest attempt is our biggest threat yet. We can clean up broken glass. We can replace burnt-up workstations. But if the abortionists succeed in revoking our doctor's licenses, it's over. **Do you want us shut down? Do you want the only medical offices available to scared, pregnant women to be run by abortion mills like Planned Parenthood?** [](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916970:6F0Q8kVNs:m:1:3253819041:8FDAE57390781D67EB95D6DD13747EA2:r "Headline")Because that's what's at stake. No more ultrasounds to show the mom her preborn child's beating heart. No more nurses praying for the moms and offering them alternatives that saves the life of their child. You are essential to our ability to keep our doors open, saving preborn lives. **[Help us fight back against the abortionists' attempts to shut us down for good with your $50, $100, or $250 tax-deductible donation today.](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916970:6F0Q8kVNs:m:1:3253819041:8FDAE57390781D67EB95D6DD13747EA2:r "Help us fight back against the abortionists' attempts to shut us down for good with your $50, $100, or $250 tax-deductible donation today.")** This is a Psalm 57 moment for us right now - we at CompassCare are in the midst of lions. But we take shelter in the shadow of HIS wings. We pray that God rebukes those who hotly pursue us as He sends for His love and faithfulness. **[That's why we're asking God's faithful like you to help us fight back the lions and continue the business of our life-saving ministry by donating $100, $500, $1,000, or what you can afford today. No amount is too small and your donation to CompassCare is tax-deductible.](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916970:6F0Q8kVNs:m:1:3253819041:8FDAE57390781D67EB95D6DD13747EA2:r "That’s why we’re asking God’s faithful like
you to help us fight back the lions and continue the business of our life-saving ministry by donating $100, $500, $1,000, or what you can afford
today. No amount is too small and your donation to CompassCare is tax-deductible.")** Don't delay. Your support can help us save the lives of countless preborn children and their mothers as combat the abortionists determined to shut us down for good. **[Donate today.](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916970:6F0Q8kVNs:m:1:3253819041:8FDAE57390781D67EB95D6DD13747EA2:r "Donate today.")** For the preborn in Christ, [](http://email.vervemail.com/ct/60916970:6F0Q8kVNs:m:1:3253819041:8FDAE57390781D67EB95D6DD13747EA2:r "Rev. James R. Harden") Rev. James R. Harden, M.Div

body:
| Peter,

**I’m so honored that Joe Cunningham has chosen me to be his running mate in the race for governor of South Carolina.**

My whole life has been about fighting for what’s right, even when it wasn’t the easiest thing to do.

When I first applied to the Air Force Academy at age 18 because I wanted to fly F-16 fighter jets, I was told that girls weren’t allowed to engage in combat. So I moved on, instead going to Princeton and then getting my law degree at the University of Virginia.

**But when that rule changed, I applied again, and ultimately became the first female fighter pilot in South Carolina, serving three combat tours in Iraq.

Now, I want to take my fighting energy and bring it to this campaign in South Carolina, delivering for working families as your Lieutenant Governor.**

But here’s the thing: We’re going up against Henry McMaster, who has spent the last four years fundraising and courting the support of special interest donors.

**[That is why I am asking for your help. Now that I am a part of the team, we have to step up. I’m proud that my young children get to see their mom breaking barriers and achieving her dreams. And I hope that my journey provides inspiration to other young women striving for things that they are told they can’t or shouldn’t do.

Today, I serve as CEO of one of South Carolina’s most esteemed law firms—a place where women make up 60% of the executive leadership team—and I’ve been recognized as one of the top 25 lawyers in the state.

Now I want to bring my skills as a fighter, a litigator, and a negotiator to the halls of government, where I can do more for the people of South Carolina. As lieutenant governor, I want to champion women’s rights, make sure our kids have access to the best education possible, and provide high-quality health care to everyone, especially our veterans.

Like many of you, I believe our great state isn’t living up to its full potential. We have leaders who are rejecting lifesaving Medicaid funds just to score political points, taking away women’s freedom to do what they want with their own bodies, and leaving our children behind.

That’s about to change. But I can’t do it alone.

clean_body: | Peter, I’m so honored that Joe Cunningham has chosen me to be his running mate in the race for governor of South Carolina. My whole life has been about fighting for what’s right, even when it wasn’t the easiest thing to do. When I first applied to the Air Force Academy at age 18 because I wanted to fly F-16 fighter jets, I was told that girls weren’t allowed to engage in combat. So I moved on, instead going to Princeton and then getting my law degree at the University of Virginia. But when that rule changed, I applied again, and ultimately became the first female fighter pilot in South Carolina, serving three combat tours in Iraq. Now, I want to take my fighting energy and bring it to this campaign in South Carolina, delivering for working families as your Lieutenant Governor. But here’s the thing: We’re going up against Henry McMaster, who has spent the last four years fundraising and courting the support of special interest donors. = | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process now. | = | = | = | = | = | = I’m proud that my young children get to see their mom breaking barriers and achieving her dreams. And I hope that my journey provides inspiration to other young women striving for things that they are told they can’t or shouldn’t do. Today, I serve as CEO of one of South Carolina’s most esteemed law firms—a place where women make up 60% of the executive leadership team—and I’ve been recognized as one of the top 25 lawyers in the state. Now I want to bring my skills as a fighter, a litigator, and a negotiator to the halls of government, where I can do more for the people of South Carolina. As lieutenant governor, I want to champion women’s rights, make sure our kids have access to the best education possible, and provide high-quality health care to everyone, especially our veterans. Like many of you, I believe our great state isn’t living up to its full potential. We have leaders who are rejecting lifesaving Medicaid funds just to score political points, taking away women’s freedom to do what they want with their own bodies, and leaving our children behind. That’s about to change. But I can’t do it alone. = I look forward to getting to know you all better over the coming months and talking about ways to change South Carolina for the better. All the best, Tally = | = | | If you'd like to receive only the most important updates from our team, Paid for by Joe Cunningham for South Carolina Joe Cunningham PO Box 21012 Charleston, SC 29413 United States **

Now, more than ever, it is critical that we strengthen the industries that support our economy. In Buncombe County, one of those major industries is tourism.

Earlier this year, it was brought to my attention that the current divide in Buncombe County's Tourism Development Authority fund was stripping the community of opportunities to improve the county to encourage longer visits by requiring the majority of funds, 75%, go towards marketing and only 25% towards local projects and venues.

These distributions have been stifling tourism and economic growth. For that reason, I worked with stakeholders across Asheville and Buncombe County to pass [House Bill 1057](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019GdQyp0MYeqsfP4Pc0X-TLKTYg_-1fr6xORDuL-YChTl0zAkNNblOTJ-S0LrYOf47ZgjAUjncmbBvhB8-usws7H74-YvzkjP4DiBqSehGIPlOh7rVL_V1TmoOu0uEIOqJQz7JqLaL1OAlIphdx0R6udWe98SmMoPalYsZgRjrPu-HPohD5_BNRjzDiqFhUWpICWf6l3fP6TmGOgUNxIoWg==&c=_65hAURnByInG0dqv2Z9_GhOIimjKtyPWesWwTl8xUrt_oZ1R21BYg==&ch=FTf7xMwG_eNym-0dj5a1YsmgcjNAg_2lhoNF7bM512QQbL9KcwlEEQ==), which redistributes TDA funds to create a 66%/33% split, granting more money towards community-oriented projects and reducing the distribution allocated towards marketing the City of Asheville. The remaining 1% will be evenly allocated towards the Tourism Product Development Fund and the Legacy Investment from Tourism Fund, both created by the TDA.

It will be enlightening to see a greater portion of taxpayer dollars directly invested back into Buncombe County to better the community for residents and visitors alike. More projects than ever will have an opportunity to be funded through the TDA, and adjusting these funds will improve both the tourism and lodging industries, producing a stronger local economy overall in Buncombe County.

I was thrilled to take the lead on this initiative and am proud we were able to get it accomplished. I look forward to watching the ways in which this redistribution will help Buncombe County thrive, and assist them in continuing to flourish as one of the leading tourism hubs in North Carolina.

** TDA funds are made up of the hotel and occupancy tax revenues in Buncombe County.

| More Money for WNC in State Budget
---
| | |
---|---
|
When I first entered the North Carolina Senate I made a promise that western NC would never get left behind. I am elated to say that this is once again true, and I have helped to secure another $26 million that will go directly into Henderson, Buncombe, and Transylvania Counties!

During this session, my colleagues and I worked diligently to craft another budget that would spend a portion of the surplus left over from the 2021 Budget. Due to the fact that we were working with a surplus and not the full annual budget, funds were limited making efforts to gain funding for localities more difficult than in traditional budget years. Nonetheless, we brought home funding to support infrastructure development, pro-life pregnancy centers, economic development projects, and other western-based non-profits.

Below is a breakdown of where all $26 million was allocated throughout District 48:
* $1M to Henderson County to use for public projects.
* $500,000 to Transylvania County to use for public projects.
* $2.75M to Buncombe County for a flood mitigation project in Barnardsville.
* $200,000 to Buncombe County for park development in Fairview.
* $500,000 in directed grants to First Contact Ministries, Inc. in Henderson County bringing their total grant to $2 million for FY 2022-23
* $500,000 in directed grants to Open Arms Pregnancy Center in Hendersonville.
* $500,000 in funding to Marketing Association for Rehabilitation Centers (MARC), Inc. a nonprofit in Fletcher, NC.
* $300,000 grant to Conserving Carolina for dam repairs in Hendersonville.
* $500,000 grant to Edneyville Volunteer Fire & Rescue, Inc. for capital improvements or equipment.
* $500,000 directed grant to Mountain Area Pregnancy Services in Buncombe County and $50,000 for services in Asheville.
* $100,000 of federal Substance Abuse Block Grant funds for First Step Farm of WNC, Inc. in Buncombe County.
* $4 million grant to Mountain Area Health Education Center for capital improvements or equipment in Asheville.

This funding coupled with original allocations in the FY 2021-23 Budget will only further assist local governments and non-profits in producing services that will further benefit the mountain folks of WNC.

While I am overwhelmingly grateful for all we have accomplished for the district, I know many of you may not be able to read this without fear for your personal, or North Carolina's, future if a recession does take place. I want to assure you that North Carolina IS prepared for a recession. We have spent the last decade working to ensure we have a hardy financial foundation to protect our economic strength in the face of a recession. This year we even went a step further by creating the "State Inflationary Reserve".

The State Inflationary Reserve puts aside $1 billion to brace for a possible recession and further allocates over $385 million to protect against economic headwinds, such as increased construction costs and other inflation. To put it succinctly: NC is prepared to handle a recession.

All in all, I am proud to have voted yes on a budget that once again gives western NC its fair share.

| Requiring Cooperation with ICE 2.0
---
| | |
---|---
|
I sponsored SB 101, which requires law enforcement to check immigration status and comply with ICE detainers when an individual is arrested for a felony or domestic violence charge, as a critical step towards further securing the safety of our communities.

Since 2019, violent crime has been on the rise across the United States. According to the Federal Bureau of Investigation, violent crime rates reached their highest peak since 2010 in 2020, at 398.5 violent crimes per 100,000 people, per year - that's roughly 1,319,046 instances of violent crime across the country in 2020 alone. This rate does not include any other felony charges for property, drug, or driving crimes.

In the US, these crimes can be attributed to three different categories of people: crimes by US-born citizens, crimes by legal immigrants, and crimes by illegal immigrants. As one might expect, violent crimes by US-born citizens constitute the highest violent crime rate among the three; however, violent crimes by illegal immigrants continue to make a significant impact on domestic safety.

Currently, in North Carolina, law enforcement agencies are not required to check or report immigration status upon arrest. In fact, Texas is the only state that actively requires the checking and reporting of immigration status. This means that we do not have statistics regarding the crime rates of illegal immigrants in NC. Nonetheless, a study of Texas arrests and convictions conducted by [PNAS](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019GdQyp0MYeqsfP4Pc0X-TLKTYg_-1fr6xORDuL-YChTl0zAkNNblOTJ-S0LrYOf4-AtHqBKjJM371RTWd2GujfDVXkV6c7rQXW6cqwfDDemfRv3v80zipJBNKOuGBOWymlFBoQU_x9NjBHce2m6NFOv-qQfQXSSIE_IGwAJju7umWyMlZbmeCA==&c=_65hAURnByInG0dqv2Z9_GhOIimjKtyPWesWwTl8xUrt_oZ1R21BYg==&ch=FTf7xMwG_eNym-0dj5a1YsmgcjNAg_2lhoNF7bM512QQbL9KcwlEEQ==) indicates a 96.2 violent crime rate per 100,000 people by illegal immigrants from 2012-2018. Research indicates this rate is roughly equitable to what we could expect of the nationwide rate.

Using this rate, it can be concluded that roughly 314,382 of the 1,252,950 violent crimes, or 25%, of all violent crimes committed in 2018 were done so by illegal immigrants. Let me repeat that - 25% of all violent crimes were committed by offenders who should not have been in this country in the first place.

Complying with ICE in NC is optional, yet many Republican-led counties have begun to do so and seen positive impacts within their communities. Expanding the requirement to all 100 counties, including the largest counties in our state with high immigrant populations such as Durham, Mecklenburg, and Wake is a logical step toward improving the safety of our communities.

Before moving on, let me clarify a few things about this bill: This bill DOES NOT target legal immigrant populations or law-abiding persons in the US. This bill only seeks to remove the most violent of illegal immigrants from our communities, arrested with felony or domestic abuse charges. This bill is necessary to prevent re-offending, to maintain the safety of our community upon arrest, and to preserve taxpayer money. Allowing illegal immigrants to infiltrate our prison system costs NC taxpayers an average of $35,000 per illegal immigrant inmate, per year. That's $35,000 that cannot go towards schools, infrastructure, fighting inflation, etc. In short, it is not our responsibility to pay for illegal immigrants to be housed in our jails after they have already caused irrevocable harm to our communities.

As a lawmaker, it is my responsibility to not only serve my constituents but also to protect them by passing legislation that shields them from harm. With our nation's ever-changing security issues, it should be our top priority to remove as many violent offenders from our streets as possible - whether they are citizens or illegal.

I fought hard to pass SB101 this short session, as a step towards tackling our increasing safety concerns, so we could begin to focus on making changes that will reduce US-born crime rates. Disappointedly, Governor Cooper chose to stifle those efforts and protect illegal immigrants over NC communities by vetoing this bill after it reached his desk.

Many of you may have received my press release yesterday regarding the veto, so I won't beat a dead horse regarding the grave error he has made, but I must say this: substantial change to domestic security must start with securing our communities from violent people who should not be there in the first place. Stop shielding violent criminals and start protecting innocent North Carolinians.

| School Choice
---
| | |
---|---
|
PARENTS KNOW BEST.

Nobody else can understand their child's needs quite like a parent can, which is why I always prioritize the right of parents to choose where their children are educated, regardless of wealth.

It all comes down to the fact that social class and financial liquidity should not be dictating factors on where a child receives their education.

For that reason, I supported the Legislature in allocating a record-high of $74.8 million towards Opportunity Scholarship funding in 2021 and laying the framework for appropriations with an annual increase of $15 million for the next 15 years. It is for this same reason, that I am even more thrilled to have supported increasing our base appropriation by $56 million from the General Fund to the Opportunity Scholarship Grant Fund Reserve. The total base appropriation will now total more than $311 million and the 2023-2024 appropriation has been similarly increased by $56 million from $120,540,000 to $176,540,000.

This investment in education access is projected to provide scholarships for over 55,000 new deserving North Carolinians at the start of the 2022 academic year, and will continue to increase its capacity to provide scholarships for an increasing number of NC families each year through 2032.

Although additional funding for Opportunity Scholarships has been deemed controversial, what is not controversial is the fact that every single student and parent should have the ability to choose where they receive their education. Parents often wish to send their child to a private school for smaller class sizes, more individual attention that allows teachers to adapt teaching styles to individual learning needs, a religious education, among more. This funding to expand Opportunity Scholarships is yet another step towards making school accessibility a reality for all NC families.

| 888 Days Later...
---
| | |
---|---
|
Can you believe it's been 874 days since COVID-19 first shutdown our State and Governor Cooper made the State of Emergency declaration?

Now, can you believe it's been 874 days since COVID-19 first shutdown our State, we've relatively returned to normal: we no longer have to wear a mask, can attend gatherings as we please, etc, yet we are still in the State of Emergency?

As exhausting as it has been watching NC's State of Emergency continue to get extended every few months while the majority of states throughout the US return to normal, it feels relieving to report that on August 15th, 2022, after 888 days, we will finally be freed from the Governor Cooper's State of Emergency.

The Governor's primary reason for keeping the emergency declaration was because DHHS wanted to ensure they had the jurisdiction to make sure health care systems had adequate staff to respond to COVID-19, despite a decrease in needs since the peak of the pandemic.

To address these concerns, in the 2022 Budget my colleagues and I were able to collaborate with DHHS to establish regulatory health freedoms that have squashed the Governor's justification for continuing the emergency declaration. State health officials now have more flexibility to protect the public outside of a State of Emergency, leaving him no other option than to officially end it.

I can't say I'm surprised it took Governor Cooper 888 days to come to his senses, but I am beyond thankful that this unnecessary abuse of executive power is finally coming to a close. We still have roughly a month left until the emergency declaration expires on August 15th, but until then I look forward to finally being able to move forward from the pandemic, putting its hardships behind us.

| More About NC's New Budget
---
| | |
---|---
|
While I am overwhelmingly proud of the money we have secured for western NC, I am equally excited about the investments my colleagues and I made across the state to support our education system, school safety, local infrastructure, and more.

If I were to recap the entire [budget](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019GdQyp0MYeqsfP4Pc0X-TLKTYg_-1fr6xORDuL-YChTl0zAkNNblOTJ-S0LrYOf4HS6EwpI1QVPq2xdZpA26vz_RJ-yP-h7ebowOkGZlsSfstHOYaGaplj1bt3Av2hpNh2saGZUwjE-m-hyZEF2jSgdwc-U41UvUgWK7_MR_ubI=&c=_65hAURnByInG0dqv2Z9_GhOIimjKtyPWesWwTl8xUrt_oZ1R21BYg==&ch=FTf7xMwG_eNym-0dj5a1YsmgcjNAg_2lhoNF7bM512QQbL9KcwlEEQ==) for you, I have a feeling some of you may get bored. Instead, I've chosen to summarize a few of the most invigorating investments made to support our state.

To begin, my colleagues and I contributed record-breaking funding totaling $4.75 billion towards North Carolina's "Rainy Day Reserve Fund". This money can be used to respond to natural disasters, to counterbalance tax cuts or lower than anticipated revenue, to support new projects that incentivize or stimulate economic growth, etc. This money ensures North Carolina stays fiscally sound if something unexpected impacts our economy.

Beyond investments in economic security, we appropriated an additional $32 million to school safety grants and $29.6 million for mental health and substance abuse programs. Between the 2021 and 2022 budgets, the school safety grant program now totals $41.7 million in funding and will support students in crisis, provide safety training, and fund equipment in schools. The mental health and substance abuse program funding will be used to support related organizations and provide critical health care to struggling people who otherwise may lack access.

This year, we've heard concerns from numerous teachers that they continue to feel undervalued. I will always be appreciative of the invaluable contributions made to help run our state, to educate our youth, and to mentor our future leaders. For that reason, my colleagues and I have provided, on average, an extra 4.2% pay raise for teachers across our state, which is in addition to previous raises provided in the 2021 Budget. Educators have an indescribably difficult job managing classrooms full of diverse students with varying needs. Their ability to balance a classroom and curriculum should never go unnoticed.

To close out my budget talk, I wanted to highlight the diligent work completed to prioritize our state's infrastructure. In the 2022 Budget, we have allocated an additional $883 million for water and wastewater infrastructure projects and another $5 million on top of the $1 billion allocated in 2021 to expand rural broadband access. The water and wastewater projects may include expanding access to county and municipality-provided resources, as well as updating outdated underground systems that are in desperate need of repair. Meanwhile, investing in expanding broadband access will close the persistent gap in connectivity between rural and urban communities. I have been lucky to see our investment in broadband already begin to payoff for WNC citizens. Since late last year, I have been working with citizens in Bat Cave, NC to facilitate the expansion of broadband to their community. I am happy to report they are expecting to be fully connected on August 1st, and I am excited to see more rural mountain communities finally receive the online access they deserve over the years to come.

If you are interested in reading more about NC's 2022 Budget, I encourage you to review my previous newsletter, [linked here](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019GdQyp0MYeqsfP4Pc0X-TLKTYg_-1fr6xORDuL-YChTl0zAkNNblOTJ-S0LrYOf4swGwcQcVUEJtHjZfOZr9AU9DJ0UvQIqBETnlLmbjVbUmrMT1M_TEqG_LpviQQyIGJIuAnFQQ0oLL75bsjPlHrQ==&c=_65hAURnByInG0dqv2Z9_GhOIimjKtyPWesWwTl8xUrt_oZ1R21BYg==&ch=FTf7xMwG_eNym-0dj5a1YsmgcjNAg_2lhoNF7bM512QQbL9KcwlEEQ==), or you can review the press release published by Senator Berger Press Shop which details FY 22-23's [new spending plan](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019GdQyp0MYeqsfP4Pc0X-TLKTYg_-1fr6xORDuL-YChTl0zAkNNblOTJ-S0LrYOf4GGJcyODBHjcIZOW4fxt6DsRGhbJtdP-yO2x1c30uObwTs-ct8XsU3Kyq206iRgGdWiKLkyKIAdMao1XKgTV8vcU258zhVtpIh_VIqV2ZxqWnZtwuIcrpP2g6lnwDJ1ztZ87lPMsj113aqq6KyyaJp_k4S64Knwr77cuieq-cl3iiENYuWpTFICIASUkFWfgneSnVs9HKET8=&c=_65hAURnByInG0dqv2Z9_GhOIimjKtyPWesWwTl8xUrt_oZ1R21BYg==&ch=FTf7xMwG_eNym-0dj5a1YsmgcjNAg_2lhoNF7bM512QQbL9KcwlEEQ==).

For 14 of the past 15 years, North Carolina has been consistently recognized as one of the top 10 states to do business in.

This year, for the first time since CNBC began publishing their "America's Top States for Business" list in 2007, North Carolina has earned the No. 1 position. In addition to being the best state for business, CNBC also found that North Carolina has the best economy in the nation.

According to CNBC, "North Carolina's solid finances are the cornerstone of the nation's top economy". The study went on to explain that "the state's credit rating is pristine; its fiscal balance is sound. Economic growth at 6.7% last year, and job growth at 3.6% were among the strongest in the nation, according to government statistics".

These No. 1 rankings are an honor, yet come as no surprise to me. My Republican colleagues and I have diligently worked to improve North Carolina's business friendliness and gain financial security since taking control of the General Assembly over a decade ago. Both No. 1 positions were earned through years of responsible conservative spending, tax reform, providing small businesses with ample opportunities for success, and supporting the growth of corporations throughout North Carolina.

It is humbling to see our hard work has led to this ranking, but it is still just the beginning of maintaining North Carolina's strong economic excellence and ensuring we provide leading incentives to attract and grow businesses throughout the best state in the nation!

We have spent the last decade working to ensure we have a hardy financial foundation to protect our economic strength in the face of a recession. This year we even went a step further by creating the "State Inflationary Reserve". The State Inflationary Reserve puts aside $1 billion to brace for a possible recession and further allocates over $385 million to protect against economic headwinds, such as increased construction costs and other inflation. To put it succinctly: NC is prepared to handle a recession. All in all, I am proud to have voted yes on a budget that once again gives western NC its fair share. | | | | Requiring Cooperation with ICE 2.0 | | | ---|--- | I sponsored SB 101, which requires law enforcement to check immigration status and comply with ICE detainers when an individual is arrested for a felony or domestic violence charge, as a critical step towards further securing the safety of our communities. Since 2019, violent crime has been on the rise across the United States. According to the Federal Bureau of Investigation, violent crime rates reached their highest peak since 2010 in 2020, at 398.5 violent crimes per 100,000 people, per year - that's roughly 1,319,046 instances of violent crime across the country in 2020 alone. This rate does not include any other felony charges for property, drug, or driving crimes. In the US, these crimes can be attributed to three different categories of people: crimes by US-born citizens, crimes by legal immigrants, and crimes by illegal immigrants. As one might expect, violent crimes by US-born citizens constitute the highest violent crime rate among the three; however, violent crimes by illegal immigrants continue to make a significant impact on domestic safety. Currently, in North Carolina, law enforcement agencies are not required to check or report immigration status upon arrest. In fact, Texas is the only state that actively requires the checking and reporting of immigration status. This means that we do not have statistics regarding the crime rates of illegal immigrants in NC. Nonetheless, a study of Texas arrests and convictions conducted by == indicates a 96.2 violent crime rate per 100,000 people by illegal immigrants from 2012-2018. Research indicates this rate is roughly equitable to what we could expect of the nationwide rate. Using this rate, it can be concluded that roughly 314,382 of the 1,252,950 violent crimes, or 25%, of all violent crimes committed in 2018 were done so by illegal immigrants. Let me repeat that - 25% of all violent crimes were committed by offenders who should not have been in this country in the first place. Complying with ICE in NC is optional, yet many Republican-led counties have begun to do so and seen positive impacts within their communities. Expanding the requirement to all 100 counties, including the largest counties in our state with high immigrant populations such as Durham, Mecklenburg, and Wake is a logical step toward improving the safety of our communities. Before moving on, let me clarify a few things about this bill: This bill DOES NOT target legal immigrant populations or law-abiding persons in the US. This bill only seeks to remove the most violent of illegal immigrants from our communities, arrested with felony or domestic abuse charges. This bill is necessary to prevent re-offending, to maintain the safety of our community upon arrest, and to preserve taxpayer money. Allowing illegal immigrants to infiltrate our prison system costs NC taxpayers an average of $35,000 per illegal immigrant inmate, per year. That's $35,000 that cannot go towards schools, infrastructure, fighting inflation, etc. In short, it is not our responsibility to pay for illegal immigrants to be housed in our jails after they have already caused irrevocable harm to our communities. As a lawmaker, it is my responsibility to not only serve my constituents but also to protect them by passing legislation that shields them from harm. With our nation's ever-changing security issues, it should be our top priority to remove as many violent offenders from our streets as possible - whether they are citizens or illegal. I fought hard to pass SB101 this short session, as a step towards tackling our increasing safety concerns, so we could begin to focus on making changes that will reduce US-born crime rates. Disappointedly, Governor Cooper chose to stifle those efforts and protect illegal immigrants over NC communities by vetoing this bill after it reached his desk. Many of you may have received my press release yesterday regarding the veto, so I won't beat a dead horse regarding the grave error he has made, but I must say this: substantial change to domestic security must start with securing our communities from violent people who should not be there in the first place. Stop shielding violent criminals and start protecting innocent North Carolinians. | | | | School Choice | | | ---|--- | PARENTS KNOW BEST. Nobody else can understand their child's needs quite like a parent can, which is why I always prioritize the right of parents to choose where their children are educated, regardless of wealth. It all comes down to the fact that social class and financial liquidity should not be dictating factors on where a child receives their education. For that reason, I supported the Legislature in allocating a record-high of $74.8 million towards Opportunity Scholarship funding in 2021 and laying the framework for appropriations with an annual increase of $15 million for the next 15 years. It is for this same reason, that I am even more thrilled to have supported increasing our base appropriation by $56 million from the General Fund to the Opportunity Scholarship Grant Fund Reserve. The total base appropriation will now total more than $311 million and the 2023-2024 appropriation has been similarly increased by $56 million from $120,540,000 to $176,540,000. This investment in education access is projected to provide scholarships for over 55,000 new deserving North Carolinians at the start of the 2022 academic year, and will continue to increase its capacity to provide scholarships for an increasing number of NC families each year through 2032. Although additional funding for Opportunity Scholarships has been deemed controversial, what is not controversial is the fact that every single student and parent should have the ability to choose where they receive their education. Parents often wish to send their child to a private school for smaller class sizes, more individual attention that allows teachers to adapt teaching styles to individual learning needs, a religious education, among more. This funding to expand Opportunity Scholarships is yet another step towards making school accessibility a reality for all NC families. If you or someone you know is interested in applying for an Opportunity Scholarship, you can follow == to review the required qualifications, how to apply, etc. | | | | 888 Days Later... | | | ---|--- | Can you believe it's been 874 days since COVID-19 first shutdown our State and Governor Cooper made the State of Emergency declaration? Now, can you believe it's been 874 days since COVID-19 first shutdown our State, we've relatively returned to normal: we no longer have to wear a mask, can attend gatherings as we please, etc, yet we are still in the State of Emergency? As exhausting as it has been watching NC's State of Emergency continue to get extended every few months while the majority of states throughout the US return to normal, it feels relieving to report that on August 15th, 2022, after 888 days, we will finally be freed from the Governor Cooper's State of Emergency. The Governor's primary reason for keeping the emergency declaration was because DHHS wanted to ensure they had the jurisdiction to make sure health care systems had adequate staff to respond to COVID-19, despite a decrease in needs since the peak of the pandemic. To address these concerns, in the 2022 Budget my colleagues and I were able to collaborate with DHHS to establish regulatory health freedoms that have squashed the Governor's justification for continuing the emergency declaration. State health officials now have more flexibility to protect the public outside of a State of Emergency, leaving him no other option than to officially end it. I can't say I'm surprised it took Governor Cooper 888 days to come to his senses, but I am beyond thankful that this unnecessary abuse of executive power is finally coming to a close. We still have roughly a month left until the emergency declaration expires on August 15th, but until then I look forward to finally being able to move forward from the pandemic, putting its hardships behind us. | | | | More About NC's New Budget | | | ---|--- | While I am overwhelmingly proud of the money we have secured for western NC, I am equally excited about the investments my colleagues and I made across the state to support our education system, school safety, local infrastructure, and more. If I were to recap the entire == for you, I have a feeling some of you may get bored. Instead, I've chosen to summarize a few of the most invigorating investments made to support our state. To begin, my colleagues and I contributed record-breaking funding totaling $4.75 billion towards North Carolina's "Rainy Day Reserve Fund". This money can be used to respond to natural disasters, to counterbalance tax cuts or lower than anticipated revenue, to support new projects that incentivize or stimulate economic growth, etc. This money ensures North Carolina stays fiscally sound if something unexpected impacts our economy. Beyond investments in economic security, we appropriated an additional $32 million to school safety grants and $29.6 million for mental health and substance abuse programs. Between the 2021 and 2022 budgets, the school safety grant program now totals $41.7 million in funding and will support students in crisis, provide safety training, and fund equipment in schools. The mental health and substance abuse program funding will be used to support related organizations and provide critical health care to struggling people who otherwise may lack access. This year, we've heard concerns from numerous teachers that they continue to feel undervalued. I will always be appreciative of the invaluable contributions made to help run our state, to educate our youth, and to mentor our future leaders. For that reason, my colleagues and I have provided, on average, an extra 4.2% pay raise for teachers across our state, which is in addition to previous raises provided in the 2021 Budget. Educators have an indescribably difficult job managing classrooms full of diverse students with varying needs. Their ability to balance a classroom and curriculum should never go unnoticed. To close out my budget talk, I wanted to highlight the diligent work completed to prioritize our state's infrastructure. In the 2022 Budget, we have allocated an additional $883 million for water and wastewater infrastructure projects and another $5 million on top of the $1 billion allocated in 2021 to expand rural broadband access. The water and wastewater projects may include expanding access to county and municipality-provided resources, as well as updating outdated underground systems that are in desperate need of repair. Meanwhile, investing in expanding broadband access will close the persistent gap in connectivity between rural and urban communities. I have been lucky to see our investment in broadband already begin to payoff for WNC citizens. Since late last year, I have been working with citizens in Bat Cave, NC to facilitate the expansion of broadband to their community. I am happy to report they are expecting to be fully connected on August 1st, and I am excited to see more rural mountain communities finally receive the online access they deserve over the years to come. If you are interested in reading more about NC's 2022 Budget, I encourage you to review my previous newsletter, ==, or you can review the press release published by Senator Berger Press Shop which details FY 22-23's ==. | | | | NC Ranked #1 in Business by CNBC | | | ---|--- | For 14 of the past 15 years, North Carolina has been consistently recognized as one of the top 10 states to do business in. This year, for the first time since CNBC began publishing their "America's Top States for Business" list in 2007, North Carolina has earned the No. 1 position. In addition to being the best state for business, CNBC also found that North Carolina has the best economy in the nation. According to CNBC, "North Carolina's solid finances are the cornerstone of the nation's top economy". The study went on to explain that "the state's credit rating is pristine; its fiscal balance is sound. Economic growth at 6.7% last year, and job growth at 3.6% were among the strongest in the nation, according to government statistics". These No. 1 rankings are an honor, yet come as no surprise to me. My Republican colleagues and I have diligently worked to improve North Carolina's business friendliness and gain financial security since taking control of the General Assembly over a decade ago. Both No. 1 positions were earned through years of responsible conservative spending, tax reform, providing small businesses with ample opportunities for success, and supporting the growth of corporations throughout North Carolina. It is humbling to see our hard work has led to this ranking, but it is still just the beginning of maintaining North Carolina's strong economic excellence and ensuring we provide leading incentives to attract and grow businesses throughout the best state in the nation! | | | | | | | | Follow me on Facebook & Twitter and visit my == for the most current legislative updates | == == == == | | | Sen. body:
I'll never tire of an opportunity to do good and to serve the most vulnerable members of my community
| | |
---
Friend: It's important for me to share my story with you about why I'm running and why this campaign means so much to me. I hope you'll give it a read.
**Back when I was a social worker, I met a young boy who was being seriously neglected at home.** He needed immediate support – but I was told it would be weeks before he could be evaluated. I didn't think he would make it until then, so I went around the red tape and got him the help he needed. I was reprimanded, but that's what it took to save his life.

I remember being so angry that the system designed to help children like him had totally failed him. **That's when I heard that the Orlando Police Department was recruiting, and I took a call to protect and serve my community, to help people like that young boy.**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/48628843/358987083/-892300846?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk3893-fr-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84Mzc4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNzVkYTFhZS1hYTExLWVkMTEtYjQ3YS0yODE4NzhiODJjMGYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bljDwZY5pmN3NHBVRQ64IIsKRzuZWHuA9diLFRVu3dM=)
Fast-forward 27 years: I was Orlando's first woman chief of police and worked tirelessly so children like that young boy I'd met as a social worker didn't have to live in fear of playing in the streets. In my last days as chief, Mayor Buddy Dyer sat me down for a chat:
**"You have to run for Congress," he told me.**

Me? A politician? I never thought of myself that way. I even laughed.
But, as I let the idea sink in, I thought about that young boy I helped as a social worker – we were still in touch three decades later. I knew he wasn’t the only one who had to overcome hardship in his childhood: 1 in 7 kids in the U.S. lives in poverty. If I could do something to help kids like him, wouldn’t it be wrong to pass up the opportunity?

That’s when I realized that I needed to run for office to help as many children and working families as I could – so that in the next generation, more children from Florida could grow up with an incredible story of opportunity like mine. Ever since then, I’ve never stopped fighting toward that goal.
**[I'll never tire of an opportunity to do good and to serve the most vulnerable members of my community, and I'm asking you to do the same. Pitch in a contribution of $5 or more now to help send me to the Senate and continue my work of building a better future for our children.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/48628844/358987084/-892300846?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk3893-fr-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84Mzc4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNzVkYTFhZS1hYTExLWVkMTEtYjQ3YS0yODE4NzhiODJjMGYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bljDwZY5pmN3NHBVRQ64IIsKRzuZWHuA9diLFRVu3dM=)**
Not a day goes by that I don't think about that child – or all of the working families who are counting on leaders like me to help them get through dark times. To thrive and not just survive.
**For me, that's what this is all about – and it's why I believe the Senate is where I can do the most good. If I win this race, Democrats can expand our Senate majority. We'll be able to extend the enhanced Child Tax Credit that's cut child poverty by more than 40%. We'll protect children from gun violence. And we'll help families keep food on the table by making groceries and gas more affordable.**
[**That's the long and short of why I'm in this race, friend. If you're ready to help me build a better future, will you donate to my campaign today?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/48628845/358987085/-892300846?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk3893-fr-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84Mzc4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNzVkYTFhZS1hYTExLWVkMTEtYjQ3YS0yODE4NzhiODJjMGYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bljDwZY5pmN3NHBVRQ64IIsKRzuZWHuA9diLFRVu3dM=)

Thanks for reading my story,

Val Demings

Did you know that nearly half of California’s top 20 largest wildfires have happened during Newsom’s Governorship?

And after four years of literally burning the state to the ground (Trinity, Napa, Lassen, Shasta, and Butte, just to name a few), you’d think California would run out of forests to burn.

Now add another two to Newsom’s list; Yosemite and Siskiyou.

Congrats Newsom.

Predictably, he is blaming it on climate change - like that helps anything in any meaningful way.

California needs a plan to stop burning, and I have that plan.

Rest assured, it has nothing to do with the words “climate crisis.”

I share briefly about this problem and the solution below.

What California needs is forest management to protect our homes, cities, businesses, and land.

So please, hear this loud and clear: Gavin Newsom has no plan.

And California cannot withstand another 10 massive forest fires in the next four years if he remains Governor.

So I need you to take this seriously, and get involved.

Californians are starting to rise up across the state and donate to my campaign because they know that we have real solutions to the wildfire crisis.

Can I count on you as well?
